Authentication

\n

Every request to the Godzilla API is authenticated with a bearer API key.

\n\n

Getting an API key

\n

Generate one from your workspace settings. Keys are scoped to a single workspace and inherit the standard rate limit described in Rate limits.

\n\n

Using the key

\n{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=curl https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY\"}}\n\n{{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Never expose a key client-side|body_html=

Verifying webhook requests

\n

Incoming webhook deliveries are authenticated differently: by a signed X-Godzilla-Signature header rather than your API key.

Building your first pipeline

This guide walks through creating a pipeline end to end: a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that ties them together.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Before you start|body_html=

You'll need an API key. See Authentication in Getting Started if you don't have one yet.

}}

1. Create a source connector

We'll pull orders from Postgres. See Connectors for the full catalog of types.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-source.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"type":"postgres","direction":"source","config":{"connection_string":"postgres://..."}}'}}

2. Create a destination connector

We'll write to Snowflake.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-destination.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"type":"snowflake","direction":"destination","config":{"account":"..."}}'}}

3. Create the pipeline

Full request/response details are in the Pipelines endpoint reference.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-pipeline.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"name":"ingest-orders","source_connector_id":"conn_pg_orders","destination_connector_id":"conn_snowflake_dw"}'}}

The pipeline starts in draft state. Activate it once you're ready to start processing events.

Next steps

args.body:
Authentication

Every request to the Godzilla API is authenticated with a bearer API key.

Getting an API key

Generate one from your workspace settings. Keys are scoped to a single workspace and inherit the standard rate limit described in Rate limits.

Using the key

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=terminal|language=bash|code=curl https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/pipelines \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY"}} {{ds:component/code-block|filename=client.go|language=go|code=import "github.com/godzilla/godzilla-go" client := godzilla.NewClient(os.Getenv("GODZILLA_API_KEY"))}} {{ds:component/alert|variant=danger|title=Never expose a key client-side|body_html=

API keys carry full workspace access. Keep them server-side only — never embed one in a mobile app, browser bundle, or public repository.

}}

Verifying webhook requests

Incoming webhook deliveries are authenticated differently: by a signed X-Godzilla-Signature header rather than your API key.

args.short_description: Create a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that connects them, end to end.
args.body:
Building your first pipeline

This guide walks through creating a pipeline end to end: a source connector, a destination connector, and the pipeline that ties them together.

{{ds:component/alert|variant=info|title=Before you start|body_html=

You'll need an API key. See Authentication in Getting Started if you don't have one yet.

}}

1. Create a source connector

We'll pull orders from Postgres. See Connectors for the full catalog of types.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-source.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"type":"postgres","direction":"source","config":{"connection_string":"postgres://..."}}'}} {{ds:component/code-block|filename=create_source.go|language=go|code=source, err := client.Connectors.Create(ctx, godzilla.ConnectorParams{ Type: "postgres", Direction: "source", Config: map[string]string{ "connection_string": "postgres://...", }, })}}

2. Create a destination connector

We'll write to Snowflake.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-destination.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v2/connectors \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{"type":"snowflake","direction":"destination","config":{"account":"..."}}'}} {{ds:component/code-block|filename=create_destination.go|language=go|code=dest, err := client.Connectors.Create(ctx, godzilla.ConnectorParams{ Type: "snowflake", Direction: "destination", Config: map[string]string{ "account": "...", }, })}}

3. Create the pipeline

Full request/response details are in the Pipelines endpoint reference.

{{ds:component/code-block|filename=create-pipeline.sh|language=bash|code=curl -X POST https://api.godzilladocs.dev/v3/pipelines \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $GODZILLA_API_KEY" \ -d '{\"name\":\"ingest-orders\",\"source_connector_id\":\"conn_pg_orders\",\"destination_connector_id\":\"conn_snowflake_dw\"}'}} {{ds:component/code-block|filename=create_pipeline.go|language=go|code=pipeline, err := client.Pipelines.Create(ctx, godzilla.PipelineParams{ Name: "ingest-orders", SourceConnectorID: "conn_pg_orders", DestinationConnectorID: "conn_snowflake_dw", })}}

The pipeline starts in draft state. Activate it once you're ready to start processing events.

Next steps

Now that events are flowing, read Error handling & recovery to see what happens when a write fails, or Monitoring & alerts to watch it run.

parts.text:
Go code examples using the official `godzilla-go` SDK have been added alongside the existing cURL examples across the three requested pages:

- **Quickstart**: Added a Go snippet demonstrating pipeline creation using `client.Pipelines.Create(...)` alongside the cURL request.
- **Authentication**: Added a Go snippet demonstrating client initialization with `godzilla.NewClient(...)` from the environment API key under the key usage section.
- **Building your first pipeline**: Added Go code examples for Step 1 (source connector creation via `client.Connectors.Create`), Step 2 (destination connector creation), and Step 3 (pipeline creation via `client.Pipelines.Create`).

All internal links have been checked and resolved to maintain site consistency.
